status: Standard Technical English governance policy; not a deployed approval engine.
state_semantics: States are derived for a requested action and context. They do not overwrite the historical issued decision.

rules.when: Evaluating permission to take an action
rules.instruction: Use the exact repository, subject revision, action, adopted baseline, bound inputs, scope, and relevant test environment.
rules.effect: unresolved context blocks the action

rules.when: Resolving an approval subject or input
rules.instruction: Verify the immutable revision and exact-byte SHA-256 through authorized access. An old approval never transfers automatically to different bytes.
rules.effect: mismatch is stale for the requested context

rules.when: Using a decision
rules.instruction: Require approved outcome, authenticated authorized decider, applicable review evidence, and satisfied prerequisites. Final document status alone is not approval.
rules.effect: pending/rejected/changes-required is not-approved

rules.when: A subject or bound input changes
rules.instruction: Mark affected uses for reassessment. Preserve the old decision as history; decide applicability to the new context before dependent work resumes.
rules.basis: Method change loop plus owner constraint
rules.effect: stale-for-context until reassessed

rules.when: A revision is claimed to be editorial only
rules.instruction: Have the authorized approver examine the exact diff and impact record. Require a recorded no-impact review and new decision bound to the new revision and inputs.
rules.effect: old decision remains bound to old bytes

rules.when: Classifying a no-impact revision
rules.instruction: Do not treat changed requirements, contracts, dependencies, technology, test expectations, policy, commitments, or generated behavior as editorial without substantive impact assessment. The worker cannot self-certify no impact.
rules.effect: uncertainty requires normal review

rules.when: Reusing downstream evidence after an upstream change
rules.instruction: Identify the transitive affected scope. For each retained item record why its behavior, coverage, assumptions, and evidence remain applicable. Reaffirm required decisions through the existing approval route.
rules.basis: Method design/refinement loop plus owner policy
rules.effect: no blanket reuse of old evidence

rules.when: A change affects unrelated approved work
rules.instruction: Allow only demonstrably unaffected, currently authorized work to continue. Do not invalidate the whole suite merely because a new revision exists elsewhere.
rules.effect: unaffected-context decisions remain usable

rules.when: A subject has a newer revision
rules.instruction: Do not silently adopt latest. Use the explicitly selected baseline. A historical revision can remain valid in its approved context unless withdrawn, revoked, expired, or made inapplicable.
rules.effect: supersession alone does not approve new bytes

rules.when: An authorized decision withdraws an artifact or revokes approval
rules.instruction: Record actor, authority, affected decision/artifact revisions, effective time, scope, reason, and replacement or recovery requirements. Recompute affected gate eligibility.
rules.effect: revoked/withdrawn scope blocks further dependent actions

rules.when: A participant changes assignment or is replaced
rules.instruction: Verify that approval was authorized when issued and is still permitted by the applicable baseline. A routine staffing change is not an implicit retroactive revocation; explicit authority expiry or revocation is assessed for its declared scope.
rules.basis: Method transient resources and governance interpretation
rules.effect: preserve legitimate historical review evidence

rules.when: An approval or test result is old
rules.instruction: Apply no universal clock-based expiry. Enforce only explicit freshness limits in its approved policy, artifact, or test plan. Expired required evidence must be refreshed.
rules.effect: expired when the explicit applicable limit is exceeded

rules.when: The environment or dependency realization changes
rules.instruction: Reassess evidence whose validity depends on it. A simulator result cannot establish required behavior against the real service.
rules.effect: affected runtime evidence becomes stale

rules.when: An implementation changes after review or testing
rules.instruction: Review and test the changed snapshot and affected interactions before relying on acceptance. A passing previous commit does not approve the submitted revision.
rules.effect: changed source requires current evidence

rules.when: Application/Test Architect revises instructions
rules.instruction: Permit changes only within supplied bounds and the current PM assignment. Preserve required review of any actual detailed-design or test-plan revision.
rules.effect: upstream changes follow their own decision route

rules.when: Solution Architect authors a decision or changes an owned baseline
rules.instruction: Obtain CEO approval without transferring system or project design accountability. Distinguish this from authorized technical review of delegated work.
rules.effect: self-authored baseline is not approved by SA alone

rules.when: A change affects schedule, cost, scope, dependencies, or resources
rules.instruction: Have SA and PM evaluate project consequences. Obtain CEO acceptance within owner bounds, or human-owner acceptance beyond them, before adopting changed commitments.
rules.effect: local design acceptance does not amend commitments

rules.when: A proposed change departs from a guideline
rules.instruction: Require strong unusual justification and human-owner approval. Do not waive directives or source absolute prohibitions.
rules.effect: ordinary approval is not a guideline waiver

rules.when: A governance version or delegation policy changes
rules.instruction: Assess impact and follow the authorized adoption/effectivity decision. Preserve the prior version and decision history; do not silently rewrite existing approvals.
rules.effect: hold only scope affected by the adopted policy

rules.when: A review or test fails
rules.instruction: Return to the appropriate preceding activity. Route changed inputs to their owners. Do not convert a failed result into conditional success or count retries as leadership rounds.
rules.effect: fail or blocked; no phase completion

rules.when: Resuming affected work
rules.instruction: Require impact assessment, all domain decisions, revalidated evidence, and a PM-authorized current assignment. An emergency or pending escalation is not a bypass.
rules.basis: owner boundaries and Method change loop
rules.effect: remain on hold until valid

rules.when: Updating progress after evidence is invalidated
rules.instruction: Keep historical reports intact. PM excludes unsupported completion from the current applicable state and assesses rework/forecast with SA; preserve actual consumed cost.
rules.basis: Method binary phase exits and tracking
rules.effect: no negative rewriting of historical effort

rules.when: Evaluating a gate with missing or unverified evidence
rules.instruction: Return blocked or reassessment-required, not pass. A known failed criterion returns fail. Scope the hold to affected actions.
rules.effect: no approval inferred from absence of failure

authority: Use the responsible approval authority, or a higher authority explicitly delegated control. Human-owner approvals remain reserved to the human owner. Workers may stop their affected work and report a problem, but cannot revoke another role’s approval.
evidence_recording: Use existing immutable change-request, review-record, decision-record, work-assignment, verification-report, and phase-exit contracts. No new runtime role or universal approver is introduced.
